prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
# Policy Document Summary

## Core Investment Framework

This document outlines a comprehensive decade-long investment programme totalling approximately £100 billion annually in capital expenditure, plus operational spending, focused on environmental transformation and social reform.

## Energy Transformation

The plan proposes transitioning to renewable energy sources including wind, solar, tidal, and geothermal power. Key measures include removing fossil fuel subsidies, implementing a carbon tax on fossil fuels, expanding electricity grid capacity, and improving energy storage systems. Nuclear power construction would be prohibited, and unconventional fossil fuel extraction banned.

## Housing Programme

The document proposes creating 100,000 new social rental homes annually, built to high energy efficiency standards. All UK homes requiring improved insulation would receive upgrades by 2030, with major heating improvements for one million homes annually. Rental reforms would include rent controls linked to local incomes and enhanced tenant protections.

## Transport Investment

Proposed changes include £2.5 billion annually for cycling and walking infrastructure, rail network expansion and electrification, local authority control over bus services, and ending new petrol and diesel vehicle sales by 2030. The document proposes cancelling a major rail project and redirecting funds to regional rail improvements.

## Industrial Transition

Plans include support for manufacturing renewable energy infrastructure, research funding for clean technologies, skills training programmes, waste reduction measures including extended product warranties, and single-use plastic bans.

## Agriculture and Land Use

The programme proposes planting 700 million trees, transitioning farming subsidies toward sustainable practices, reducing pesticide use by 50%, supporting organic and mixed farming methods, and implementing flood management through natural measures.

## Income Support

A Universal Basic Income would replace most existing benefits, providing £89 weekly for adults and £178 for pensioners, with supplements for disabled people, lone parents, and families with children.

## Healthcare

NHS funding would increase by £6 billion annually, with privatisation rolled back and mental health services expanded. Community health centres would be established focusing on preventative care.

## Education

Schools would receive £4 billion additional annual funding, with reduced class sizes and curriculum flexibility. University tuition fees would be abolished, and existing student debt written off.

## Local Government

Councils would receive £10 billion additional funding annually, plus a £3 billion climate adaptation fund. Local authorities would gain control over bus services and housing targets.

## Democratic Reform

Proposals include proportional voting systems for parliamentary and local elections, votes at 16, an elected upper legislative chamber, and media ownership limits.

## Tax Reform

Income taxes would be consolidated, corporation tax increased to 24%, and property taxes restructured through a Land Value Tax replacing existing property-based taxes.

## International Policy

Foreign aid would increase from 0.7% to 1% of national income, with debt relief for the poorest countries and technology transfer to support climate adaptation globally.

## Animal Welfare

Measures include banning hunting, ending badger culling, restricting live animal exports, and establishing an animal protection commission.

## Drug Policy

The document proposes replacing prohibition with regulated drug access, treating addiction as a health matter, and establishing safe consumption facilities.

## Financing

The programme would be funded through carbon taxation (estimated £76.7 billion annually), income tax consolidation (£21.7 billion), corporation tax increases (£12 billion), savings from cancelled projects (£29.4 billion), and £94.4 billion annual borrowing for capital investment.
